question_text: CONNECT: 1. Marcus Trescothick 2. Khaled Mashud 3. Andrew Symonds 4. Azhar Ali 5. Travis Head. What connects these five cricketers? Hint: "If I don't reach there, I will be disappointed." - Harbhajan Singh.
answer_text: 600th Test Wickets - Shane Warne, Muttiah Muralitharan, Anil Kumble, James Anderson, Stuart Broad.

question_text: Japanese 'curry' likely came from India, but not from Indians. The consensus among historians is that Japanese curry is an adaptation of recipes and spice mixes brought over from India by 19th century British soldiers and merchants. Japanese curry (Kare), with its milder flavor profile and thicker, stew-like consistency, differs substantially from authentic Indian-style curry. In Japan, Indian curry is referred to as 'Indo Karii', to distinguish it from the Japanese variant. This naming convention is most likely down to the Soma family, whose son-in-law X invented this dish in 1927, modifying his favorite chicken curry recipe, as he attempted to diversify his in-laws' struggling bakery business. This 'new' dish became an instant hit and is today an integral part of Japanese cuisine and culture. Give the unlikely culinarian X. Hint: X made a great escape from India in a manner very similar to his namesake a generation later.

X was originally constructed by the Soviet Union in the 1950s, and they retained de facto control until their collapse in 1991. X had become strategically critical for the USSR as the region spiraled out of control in the 1970s. After the USSR, control of X was heavily contested in the ensuing civil war. Surprisingly given its centrality to the United States, X was actually secured by UK Navy Special Forces in 2001, who then handed over control to the US. X quickly expanded to become the epicenter of US operations in the region. Many US Presidents have visited X, including Eisenhower, W. Bush, Obama (4x) and Trump. The US relinquished control of X in 2021, leaving in the dead of the night without informing the local government, leading to massive looting. In August 2025, X re-entered the news cycle when Trump claimed, among other things, that "X has the most powerful _____ ever built in terms of weight, length and load of what it could take", which, he alleged, the Biden Administration "gave up for nothing". Give X. Hint: Located very close to Kabul, X was the largest US military base in Afghanistan during the war on terror.

Grieving the 1989 death of his fiancé at the hands of a drunk driver, James O'Barr created The Crow comic book series as a means of therapy and catharsis. In what is perhaps a tragic irony, Brandon Lee (the younger brother of Bruce Lee), who played the lead in the film adaptation, was accidentally killed while filming the pivotal scene. The Crow is the inspiration for X, a mild-mannered singer and guitarist who developed a hit album called 'Crow Music'. Jealous of his fame and popularity, his rivals torture and kill him. X's pet crow Prince is inconsolable at his death, and uses its powers to resurrect X. It is always sitting on his tombstone and lets out a shrill cry each time evil occurs, turning X's body into a superhuman and fearsome dispenser of justice. X himself was named after yet another legendary music composer, arranger, and teacher to many. Give X. Hint: X is named after the renowned guru of Pyarelal Sharma.
answer_text: Anthony (Anthony Gonsalvez) - an Indian comic book superhero (shown on a Raj Comics cover).

question_text: Once X was criticizing politicians who had defected from the Y party to rival outfits. X claimed that these persons were opportunistic and greedy, and predicted that they would be powerless in their new parties. Likening the statements of colleagues-turned rivals to the cries of animals, X said "A few naughty cows have left the party to join ______, -…..They are now making a lot of noise —……...The sooner they leave the party, the better." During this tirade, a seven second clip of X uttering a string of rhythmic, alliterative phrases went viral, triggering a huge meme fest and inspiring many adaptations, remixes and song integrations. Give funda. (I don't need X or Y). Hint: X gave this speech while campaigning in Murshidabad for the 2021 West Bengal Assembly elections.
answer_text: Mamata Banerjee and the 'Hamba Hamba Kamba Kamba' meme.

question_text: X was born into a middle-class family in Calcutta in 1917, at a time when women's education was not a priority in middle-class families. However, her doctor father was extremely supportive of her educational aspirations, though he likely never imagined she'd get this far. Building on a childhood interest in the medicinal properties of plants, she graduated with a degree in organic chemistry in 1936. She went on to study further, completing her doctorate in medicinal and synthetic organic chemistry from Calcutta University in 1944. During her PhD she worked with legends such as SN Bose and Acharya PC Ray. However, most people remember her as the first ever woman to earn a doctorate from an Indian university. She also became the first ever woman recipient of the Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Award in 1961. A Google doodle commemorated her 100th birth anniversary in 2017. Name this pioneering scientist X. Hint: Initials A.C., known for her research on alkaloid compounds and their therapeutic properties, developed many anti-epileptic drugs (e.g. Ayush-56, which is still in use).

A combination of the Greek words for ending and study, X concerns the study of the end times, be it the end of the current order, human life, or the universe itself. All major world religions predict that world events, especially negative ones, reach a climax, resulting in the end of the world. Abrahamic religions follow a linear cosmology, emphasizing transformation and redemption in their end times stories. These include the return of the exiled Jewish diaspora to Israel, the period before the second coming of Christ, and the Day of Judgment in Islam. In contrast, Indic religions postulate more cyclic trends, with their X expounding on themes of decay, redemption and rebirth. In the modern era, several secular and science-based X theories have popped up concerning the end of the Universe, such as the 'Big Crunch', the 'Big Rip', the 'Big Bounce' or the 'Big Freeze' (heat death). Science-based X also consider the impact of Artificial Intelligence-induced societal changes, and the so-called 'Singularity'. X expectedly finds extensive mention in science fiction, too. The ancient Greeks used the noun-form of X to denote cities and settlements at the farthest reaches of the Hellenic world. One noteworthy settlement named after X is located in modern-day Tajikistan. Hint: The noun-form of X is also the name of an album by the Polish death metal band, Behemoth. X is also the name of the superintelligence in the Charles Stross novel Singularity Sky, and the name of a series of sci-fi novels by Frederik Pohl.

In Hinduism, X is the celestial bow of Lord Shiva. X finds mention in the Yajurveda, where X is referenced multiple times, and names such as X-paani (Wielder of the X) and X-vaasa (One who wears X as an ornament). X features in several stories and legends. Shiva used the X against Lord Ganesha in the well-known story about Ganesha standing guard during Parvati's bath. Shiva also used X to annihilate the cities of the demon Tripurasura. In the Ramayana, Rama is asked to break the X as a condition for winning Sita's hand in marriage. In recognition of the immense power of X, it is also the name of India's most advanced multiple rocket launcher artillery system. Just give X. Hint: X is also the name of an upcoming Kannada movie starring Ganesh. The X veena is named after X and is similar to the modern Rudra veena.

The ______ were an ancient Indo-Aryan tribe with homelands believed in modern day Pakistan. They are an important part of the narrative of the Rig Veda and are mentioned as one of the tribes that fought Sudas in the Battle of the Ten Kings. It is mentioned thus, "Together came the ________, the Bhalanas, the Alinas, the Sivas, the Visanins. Yet to the Trtsus came the Ārya's Comrade, through love of spoil and heroes' war, to lead them." - Rigveda, Book 7, Hymn 18, Verse 7. The Greeks similarly referred to these peoples as 'Pactyans'. The ______ are believed to have eventually migrated westwards and settled in modern-day Kandahar, which is also a major center of X culture. By what name do we know the descendants? Hint: This ethnic group exerts substantial influence in the politics and culture of both Afghanistan and Pakistan.

A certain 1940s insurance agent used a business card with the following details: Name: Muhammad Ziauddin; Qualifications: B.A., LL.B.; Designation: Travelling Inspector; Company: The Empire of India Life Assurance Co. Ltd; Residence: Jubbulpore. Who was this mysterious 'agent'? Hint: Timeline hint - January 1941, Calcutta.
answer_text: Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose (the alias he used during his escape from house arrest in Calcutta in January 1941).

question_text: A recent profile of this eminent scientist X: "It is rare for someone to be a competent researcher as well as able to navigate sometimes cutthroat corporate politics. Because he can do both, currently 49-year-old X is one of the most influential technologists working on artificial intelligence today. X is currently CEO of Google DeepMind, an organization with notable research capabilities demonstrated by their many technical firsts spanning over a decade of AI research. Such research capacity is surprisingly rare in the crowded field of giant companies eagerly contending to lead the AI industry, perhaps matched by only a few other exceptions such as OpenAI and DeepSeek. For example, under X, DeepMind built the program AlphaFold to predict protein structures, for which Hassabis was awarded the 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry and was knighted in the United Kingdom." Hint: Initials D.H.

This word X, derived from the Old Norse for "to swing", was originally used as British thieves' slang to describe stolen valuables, such as jewelry. It now connotes any piece of stylish or flashy clothing, jewelry or accessory. In America, it can also mean free gifts or goodies that one receives in conferences, promotional events and job fairs, for example. It's also used to denote confidence and stylishness in general. What word? Hint: Four-letter word; a certain Pooja sings about how Desi her X is.

One element in this seal is the Goddess Isis Pharia, protector of sailors, standing on a ship and holding a scroll. With this information and other clues in this picture, identify this seal and emblem. The image shows a coat-of-arms/seal topped with a castle-wall crown and an Arabic text banner, with a shield depicting the goddess figure standing beside a lighthouse tower above wavy water. Hint: This organization is headquartered at its namesake in Northern Virginia (shown alongside the unrelated seal of the United States Patent and Trademark Office as a wordplay hint).
answer_text: Alexandria, Egypt. The Arabic text reads 'Governorate of Iskandariya', the Arabic name for the city and province. The legendary Pharos Lighthouse is also shown on the seal.
